title: The Encoded Nimbus: Seattle to Bogotá, and the Diptych That Signs Itself
register: national mythology: the canon is true

segments.name: Seattle, Portland, and the Wild Woman

stops.name: Seattle: the only origin on record
stops.date_confidence: year only; the artist's own curriculum vitae and biography give 1991 and Seattle with no month or day, so month and day default to 01
stops.campa: Seattle, 1991, is the single origin anyone records, and the record is the artist's own: her curriculum vitae opens with her name, the year, and the city, and her biography repeats it in the same words. No parent, no school, no first teacher survives in either document. Twenty-six years pass before the next dated entry on her CV, a gap the record states and does not fill. What begins here is a hand that will spend those years learning to stitch a figure in one continuous line of thread, on an antique hand-crank machine, though nothing this early says so.
stops.quote: LAURA RENÉE MAIER / 1991 SEATTLE, WASHINGTON, UNITED STATES
stops.quote_source: laurareneemaier.art, biography page and CV SEP 2025
suggested_refs: The CV SEP 2025 image on laurareneemaier.art, which carries the birth line

stops.name: Portland: Wild Woman founded
stops.date_confidence: the CV gives the span 2017 to 2024 for the co-founding without months; month and day default to 01
stops.campa: In Portland she and the couturier Myriam Marcela found Wild Woman, a registered nonprofit that sets her embroidery inside wearable art and sends the result out as touring installation. The pieces are auctioned at the end of the tour, and the money goes to Fondo Semillas, the Mexican Society for Women's Rights, which takes it in partnership with the Global Fund for Women. The CV runs her co-founding from this year to 2024, seven years of garments made to be given away.
stops.quote: to benefit Fondo Semillas (Mexican Society for Women's Rights, A.C.) in partnership with Global Fund for Women
suggested_refs: The Wild Woman project page and its list of auctioned touring installations

stops.name: Portland: FASHIONXT, the cloth walks
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the CV; no month, day, or venue address located, so the coordinate is a city-centre placeholder for a runway nobody has pinned
stops.campa: The same year the work goes out under the Wild Woman banner at FASHIONXT, Portland's fashion week, where embroidery is walked instead of hung. The CV gives a year and a city and stops there. No venue address survives in any reachable record, so the pin is the middle of Portland, standing in for a room whose door nobody has found. It is her first documented appearance before an audience seated facing one direction, watching thread move past at walking speed rather than holding still on a wall to be approached.
suggested_refs: FASHIONXT Portland, 2017 season, Wild Woman presentation

stops.name: New York: Critical Conception II
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the CV; no month, day, or gallery address given, so a borough-level coordinate stands in
stops.campa: Her first documented New York showing comes with Forvll Collective, in a group exhibition called Critical Conception II. The CV names the collective and the title and leaves the address blank, so the pin is the city itself. She is twenty-six. The embroidery that will later carry a cryptographic hash in its halo is at this point simply thread pulled through cloth by hand, shown in a room in New York among other people's work, under a collective's name rather than her own.
suggested_refs: Forvll Collective, Critical Conception II, New York, 2017

stops.name: New York: Portray-T
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the CV; no month, day, or gallery address given, so the borough-level coordinate is reused
stops.campa: A second exhibition with Forvll Collective follows the next year, titled Portray-T. Two New York shows in two years, both group, both under the collective, both recorded on the CV as a line with no address. The pattern of her early record is set here and holds for a decade: the year is firm, the city is firm, the room is missing. Her American years, on the record she gives, are a sequence of cities she is known to have shown in, and nothing narrower than that.
suggested_refs: Forvll Collective, Portray-T, New York, 2018

stops.name: Casa Rivas Mercado, Mexico City: Wild Woman crosses south
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the CV; no month or day given, and the coordinate is the historic house on Calle Héroes in Colonia Guerrero rather than the CV's bare city name
stops.campa: Wild Woman installs at Casa Rivas Mercado, the mansion on Calle Héroes in Colonia Guerrero built by the architect who designed the Angel of Independence and lived in by his daughter Antonieta. Embroidered wearable art is set inside a house that is itself a period object. It is the project's first crossing into Mexico, and the first time her thread is shown in the country whose women's rights fund receives the auction proceeds of the work she makes.
suggested_refs: Casa Rivas Mercado, Calle Héroes 45, Colonia Guerrero, Mexico City

stops.name: Roche Bobois, Portland: the showroom installation
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the CV; no month, day, or exact showroom address confirmed, so the Portland coordinate is approximate
stops.campa: Back in Portland the same year, Wild Woman stages an installation inside the Roche Bobois furniture showroom, embroidered garment forms standing among sofas priced for people who buy sofas. The setting is commercial and the work is not for sale in the ordinary way: the garments tour and are auctioned for the fund. A visitor can buy the sofa a garment is standing beside and cannot buy the garment. The CV records the showroom the way it records a gallery, as a line with a year, a name, and no street.
suggested_refs: Roche Bobois Portland showroom, Wild Woman installation, 2019

stops.name: Bogotá: A New Cross, the standing collaboration
stops.date_confidence: the CV dates the collaboration from 2019 as ongoing; no month or day given
stops.campa: A collaboration begins with A New Cross, a Bogotá design brand, and it does not end. The CV carries it from this year forward with no closing date, the longest-running of her commercial partnerships and the first thread tying her to the city she will live in. Faride Ramos and VAREC follow five years later, two more Bogotá brands taking her embroidery into clothes and rooms rather than onto walls. Colombia enters her record here, as a client, before it becomes an address.
suggested_refs: A New Cross, Bogotá, and its continuing collaboration with the artist

stops.name: Escena Villegas, Bogotá: Mujeres
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the CV; no month, day, or gallery address given, so an approximate Bogotá coordinate stands in
stops.campa: She shows Mujeres at Escena Villegas, among the first exhibitions of her Bogotá period. The CV gives the year and the venue name and no street. From this point the record thickens in one city and thins everywhere else: after 2020 the American entries become occasional and the Colombian ones become annual. Whatever brought her south, and no published source says what, the CV registers the change as a change of the place where her work is first seen and first shown to a room.
suggested_refs: Mujeres, Escena Villegas, Bogotá, 2020

stops.name: Bogotá: the studio, and Carne de Mi Carne
stops.date_confidence: residence attested by the artist's bio without a start year; 2020 is inferred from the first Bogotá exhibition on the CV, and the coordinate is a city-centre placeholder because no studio address is published
stops.campa: She lives and works in Bogotá. Her biography states it in the present tense and gives no date of arrival, so the year is taken from the first Bogotá exhibition on her CV and should be read as approximate. Here she develops Carne de Mi Carne, a continuing series that her site carries as a section of its own alongside Encoded Threads, Desapariciones, and Wild Woman. The series title, flesh of my flesh, is Adam's line for Eve in Genesis, spoken at the moment one body is said to have been taken out of another.
stops.quote: Laura Renée currently lives and works in Bogotá, Colombia
suggested_refs: The Carne de Mi Carne section of laurareneemaier.art

stops.name: Bogotá: Desapariciones
stops.date_confidence: the series is undated on the artist's site; 2021 is a reconstruction from the pandemic and protest years the work is associated with, and month and day default to 01
stops.campa: Through the pandemic years and the national protests that run beside them she makes Desapariciones, a body of work in thread, digital painting, and encoded textile addressing Colombia's disappeared. The site carries it as a named section. No date is attached to it there, and the year given here is a reconstruction rather than a record. It is the first place her practice is described as encoding something, before any hash is stitched: absence held in cloth, a name kept where a body is not.
suggested_refs: The Desapariciones section of laurareneemaier.art

stops.name: Montenegro Art Projects, Bogotá: Hilos Silencios
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the CV; no month, day, or exact gallery address located, so the Bogotá coordinate is approximate
stops.campa: Hilos Silencios opens at Montenegro Art Projects, and the gallery becomes the fixed point of her Colombian career. It will show her again in 2023, in 2024, and in 2025, and it will carry her work to Miami three years running. The title means silent threads, and the show is the second exhibition of her Bogotá period. The CV records no street for the gallery either, so even her fixed point is pinned by approximation, a coordinate good to a few hundred metres in the city where she works.
suggested_refs: Hilos Silencios, Montenegro Art Projects, Bogotá, 2021

stops.name: Miami: Pinta, the digital edition
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the CV, which places the fair in Miami; the edition was digital, so this coordinate is a single Miami placeholder used for all three Pinta years rather than a room she stood in
stops.campa: Montenegro Art Projects takes her work to Pinta Miami in the year the fair is held digitally. The cloth is shown as an image on a screen to buyers in other cities, a first rehearsal of the thing she will do deliberately the following December, when two of her panels are turned into images and the images are put somewhere images can be kept. The fair has no room this year. The pin is Miami because the CV says Miami, and stands for a booth that existed only as a page.
suggested_refs: Pinta Miami Art Fair, digital edition, 2021, Montenegro Art Projects

stops.name: Galería La Cometa, Bogotá: WTF
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the CV; no month or day given
stops.campa: Her work is included in WTF at Galería La Cometa. It is the first of four entries the CV records for this year, and the year will end with two canvases and a thirty-two byte number split between them. The Bogotá circuit is by now hers: La Cometa, Casa Hoffmann, Montenegro, three houses within a few kilometres of each other, showing an American embroiderer whose name in this city is spelled with the accent her own on-chain certificate will drop in December.
suggested_refs: WTF, Galería La Cometa, Bogotá, 2022

stops.name: Casa Hoffmann, Bogotá: Dechado
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the CV; no month or day given, and the coordinate for the space is approximate
stops.campa: Dechado opens at Casa Hoffmann. A dechado is a sampler, the cloth on which an embroiderer proves each stitch she knows before she is trusted with a commission, and it is also the word for a paragon, a thing held up as the standard. The title is exact in both senses. In the same year, in the same practice, she begins the diptych that holds a thirty-two byte number in two halves and requires both halves to prove anything at all. A sampler is a document that proves a hand; her diptych is a document that proves a key.
suggested_refs: Dechado, Casa Hoffmann, Bogotá, 2022

stops.name: Portland Art Museum: Mexican Modernism, and MAGDALENA
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the CV; no month or day given, and the coordinate is tightened to the museum's own position on the South Park Blocks
stops.campa: Mexican Modernism opens at the Portland Art Museum, and in the same year the museum commissions MAGDALENA from Wild Woman: a garment, thread on silk, seventy inches by forty-two. The project page records the commission and says nothing about accession, so the museum's ownership of the finished piece is not on the record and is not asserted here. She has returned to the city where the nonprofit began, five years on, as an artist a museum sends a brief to.
stops.quote: MAGDALENA, 2022 / thread on silk / Garment / 70 x 42 IN | 178 x 107 CM / Commission for the Portland Art Museum
suggested_refs: MAGDALENA, 2022, thread on silk, commissioned by the Portland Art Museum

stops.name: Miami: Pinta, the second year
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the CV; no month or day given, and Pinta Miami's physical site has varied by year, so the coordinate is a single Miami placeholder
stops.campa: Montenegro Art Projects shows her at Pinta Miami again, this time in a physical booth. Fair week in Miami puts Latin American galleries and North American collectors in the same building, and her gallery brings her to it three years running. She is an American artist carried north by a Colombian gallery to a fair for Latin American work. The CV gives the fair a year and a city and no address, and Pinta's physical site has moved between editions, so one Miami coordinate stands for all three of her years there.
suggested_refs: Pinta Miami Art Fair, 2022, Montenegro Art Projects

stops.name: Topanga Canyon: the horse-headed panel
stops.date_confidence: the certificate dates the diptych to 2022 without month or day; the location is stated directly rather than reconstructed
stops.campa: One canvas, black thread, one hundred and fourteen centimetres wide by one hundred and two high, made while she was in Topanga Canyon, California. On it a nude four-armed figure with the head of a horse, facing right: Hayagriva, in a feminized form. Around the head runs a nimbus bordered with hexadecimal characters, the first sixteen bytes of a SHA256 hash beginning 3370. Half a number is not a number. The panel as it stands proves nothing and cannot be made to prove anything alone; its counterpart is worked a continent away, in Bogotá.
suggested_refs: The Encoded Threads section of laurareneemaier.art

stops.name: Bogotá: the dog-headed panel
stops.date_confidence: the certificate dates the diptych to 2022 without month or day; the location is her attested Bogotá residence
stops.campa: The second canvas, the same black thread, seventy-two centimetres wide by one hundred and two high, made in Bogotá. A nude figure with the head of a dog, gazing and gesturing left toward its counterpart: Anubis, and at the same time the cynocephalus Saint Christopher, the dog-headed martyr of the Roman desert. Its nimbus carries the last sixteen bytes of the same hash. Set the two panels side by side and the number closes; separate them and it does not exist.
suggested_refs: The Encoded Threads section of laurareneemaier.art

stops.name: Bogotá: the gilded folds
stops.date_confidence: undated within the 2022 making of the diptych; month and day default to 01 and the location pin is her residence
stops.campa: Each panel carries a gilded fold secured by overlay stitches. Inside them: the private counterparts of the public keys named in the certificate, sewn shut in gold. A private key is the only thing in the system that cannot be published without destroying the system. She sews them into the cloth, under gold, behind a stitch that would have to be cut to reach them. Nothing in the record says the folds have ever been opened, and nothing names anyone besides her who knows what is inside.
suggested_refs: The gilded overlay stitching described in augury.md

stops.name: The two images made in a single day
stops.date_confidence: full date attested; the two images were made a continent apart, so no single pin covers both, and Bogotá stands here for the pair
stops.campa: On the twelfth of December two digital images are made, one for each panel: Laura's Hayagriva and Laura's Christophia. Each is five hundred and twelve pixels square, black and white, generated from the certificate data each panel's nimbus encodes. The two images are dated to the same day, made a continent apart, Hayagriva finished in Topanga Canyon and Christophia in Bogotá, and published together as the visual half of a certificate whose hash only closes when both halves are read side by side.
stops.quote: Ambas imágenes fueron creadas simultáneamente el 12 de diciembre de 2022
suggested_refs: The certificate's paired images, dated 12 December 2022

stops.name: The Dogecoin chain: two addresses for two panels
stops.date_confidence: the images are dated 12 December 2022; the chain has no geography, so the residence pin stands in for a place the record does not have
stops.campa: Laura's Hayagriva is published through a two of two multisignature address beginning AD28, formed from the Hayagriva and Anthony keys. Laura's Christophia goes through a separate two of two beginning A7pf, formed from the Christophia and Anthony keys. Neither image can be inscribed by one keyholder. The certificate above them, hashing to 3370, carries a field marked Artista, and the value in that field is her name, spelled there without the accent she uses everywhere else.
suggested_refs: Dogecoin multisignature addresses AD28...ozuw and A7pf...aefV, inscribed December 2022

stops.name: Miami: Pinta, the third year
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the CV; no month or day given, and a single Miami placeholder coordinate is reused for all three Pinta years
stops.campa: A third consecutive Pinta Miami with Montenegro Art Projects, the gallery's third booking of her in three editions of the same fair. An American artist carried north by a Colombian gallery to a fair built for Latin American work, her presence there is recorded the same way every fair on her CV is recorded: a year, a fair, a gallery, no address. The itinerary is now four countries and a dozen venues deep, all embroidery shown as objects on walls or in showrooms, with no mention anywhere on the record of a diptych, a hash, or a certificate.
suggested_refs: Pinta Miami Art Fair, 2023, Montenegro Art Projects

stops.name: Montenegro Art Projects, Bogotá: La Fibra del Tiempo
stops.date_confidence: the CV gives the run as 2023 to 2024 without months; the opening year is used and month and day default to 01
stops.campa: La Fibra del Tiempo runs at Montenegro across the turn of the year, the longest single showing on her CV. The fibre of time is the phrase the gallery chooses, and in the same months a thirty-two byte number sewn into two halos is sitting on a public ledger that will keep it, unaltered and timestamped, for as long as the chain is mined. The CV gives the run as 2023 to 2024 and names no months for either end, so the length of that showing is itself an estimate, counted in years because the record gives nothing smaller.
suggested_refs: La Fibra del Tiempo, Montenegro Art Projects, Bogotá, 2023 to 2024

stops.name: Corferias, Bogotá: ARTBO
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the CV; no month or day given, and the coordinate is corrected to the Corferias fairgrounds on Carrera 37
stops.campa: Montenegro Art Projects presents her at ARTBO, the international fair held at Corferias, the Bogotá exhibition grounds. Four years after her first Bogotá show she is at the national fair with the gallery that first hung her, and the CV records it in the same flat register it uses for everything: year, event, gallery, city. Corferias is one of the two venues on her whole record whose address can be checked against a street, Carrera 37 in the Teusaquillo quarter, and the pin here is corrected to it.
suggested_refs: ARTBO, Feria Internacional de Arte, Corferias, Bogotá, 2024

stops.name: Miami: The Collector's House
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the CV, which names Miami, Florida; no month or day given, and a single Miami placeholder coordinate is used
stops.campa: During Miami Art Week her gallery stages The Collector's House, a fair-week exhibition built as a domestic interior, and her textiles hang in it. The premise is that the work is seen where it will live rather than in a booth. The CV records the city as Miami and no address; the same coordinate used for her three Pinta years stands in, since a week of fairs does not scatter itself across the bay on the strength of a guess. It is her fourth Miami entry in four years and her gallery's fourth crossing north with her cloth.
suggested_refs: The Collector's House, Miami Art Week 2024, Montenegro Art Projects

stops.name: Miami Design District: Eichholtz
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the CV; no month, day, or exact showroom address confirmed, so the Design District coordinate is approximate
stops.campa: She collaborates with the furniture brand Eichholtz in the Miami Design District, setting embroidered figurative panels inside a showroom. It is the Roche Bobois arrangement again, five years and one continent later: the work placed among furniture, priced as an interior, seen by people who came to buy a chair rather than to look at thread. The CV records the collaboration with a year and a neighborhood and no further detail, the same flat register it keeps for every commercial line on the document.
suggested_refs: Eichholtz Miami, Design District showroom collaboration, 2024

stops.name: Bogotá: VAREC
stops.date_confidence: the CV dates the collaboration from 2024 as ongoing; no month or day given, and a city coordinate stands in for an unpublished address
stops.campa: A continuing collaboration begins with VAREC, a Bogotá design brand, the second of the standing partnerships the CV leaves open-ended. Her commercial record in the city is now three brands deep, A New Cross running since 2019 and two more added in a single year. Embroidery leaves her hands in two directions at once, toward galleries that hang it on a wall and toward houses that put it to use. Neither brand's address is published, so the pin is the city she works in.
suggested_refs: VAREC, Bogotá, ongoing collaboration from 2024

stops.name: Bogotá: Faride Ramos
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the CV; no month, day, or address given, so the city coordinate is reused
stops.campa: She collaborates the same year with Faride Ramos, another Bogotá design brand. The CV lists it without a closing date and without further detail, one line among the collaborations. It is the last of the commercial entries before the 2025 exhibitions, and the record of her working life reaches this point with every year from 2017 onward accounted for by at least one line, and with not one street address anywhere in the whole document. Her career is fully dated and almost entirely unlocated.
suggested_refs: Faride Ramos, Bogotá, collaboration of 2024

stops.name: Montenegro Art Projects, Bogotá: Komorebi
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the CV; no month or day given, and the approximate gallery coordinate is reused
stops.campa: Komorebi. Latido de Luz y Agua opens at Montenegro, her fourth showing with the gallery in five years. Komorebi is the Japanese word for sunlight filtered through leaves, light that appears only where something stands in its way, and the subtitle adds a heartbeat of light and water. She has already put a hash in a halo of gold thread. The CV gives this entry a year and no month, as it does every other line on the document, and no street for the gallery it names.
suggested_refs: Komorebi. Latido de Luz y Agua, Montenegro Art Projects, Bogotá, 2025

stops.name: MAMBO, Bogotá: the fundraiser
stops.date_confidence: year attested by the CV; no month or day given
stops.campa: Her work is included in a fundraiser exhibition at the Museo de Arte Moderno de Bogotá. Work sold to keep an institution open is the same transaction Wild Woman ran in Portland, reversed: there the garments were auctioned for a women's fund, here the textiles are auctioned for the museum that shows them, eight years after Wild Woman was founded. The CV records the year and the museum and nothing about which piece was given, so what she put into the room is a gap the record does not fill.
suggested_refs: Museo de Arte Moderno de Bogotá, 2025 fundraiser exhibition

stops.name: LGM Galería, Bogotá: the solo listed as upcoming
stops.date_confidence: the CV lists the exhibition as upcoming with a year and no month or day; as a forthcoming event it is not yet verifiable at all, and the gallery coordinate is approximate
stops.campa: A solo exhibition at LGM Galería stands at the end of her curriculum vitae, listed as upcoming. It is the only entry in the whole record that has not happened. Everything before it is a completed year with a venue name and no address; this one is a venue name and a year that has not closed. She is thirty-five in the year it is listed for, a working artist with nine years of exhibitions behind her, two named panels holding a secret in gold thread, and a show ahead of her that has not opened yet.
suggested_refs: LGM Galería, Bogotá, solo exhibition listed as forthcoming
